stimuli.text: Researchers collected data from 1,000 students. For each one, they recorded intelligence test score at age 11 and average school grade at age 16. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.60.

Researchers investigated whether the wording of a question changes what witnesses remember. They recruited 100 adult volunteers who watched a film of a car accident and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they smashed into each other. Participants in the other condition were asked how fast the cars were going when they contacted each other. The researchers then recorded the speed in kilometers per hour that each participant wrote down.

Researchers investigated whether a new drug reduces anxiety. They recruited 150 adults diagnosed with generalized anxiety disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition took the new drug every day for eight weeks. Participants in the other condition took a placebo pill that looked identical every day for eight weeks. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard anxiety questionnaire after eight weeks.

Researchers collected data from 1,200 teenagers. For each one, they recorded the number of hours of social media use per day and score on a depression questionnaire. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.28.

Researchers collected data from 400 high school students. For each one, they recorded the average number of hours slept per night and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.45.

Researchers investigated whether a night without sleep slows reaction time. They recruited 60 adult volunteers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition stayed awake all night in the laboratory. Participants in the other condition slept for eight hours in the laboratory. The researchers then recorded the average time in milliseconds that each participant took to press a button when a light appeared. The results are shown in the table. The difference between the two groups had a p value of 0.41.

rows.group: The group that stayed awake all night
The group that slept for eight hours

stimuli.text: Researchers investigated whether the presence of other people slows the reporting of an emergency. They recruited 80 university students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition were filling in a form in a room with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants in the other condition were filling in the form alone when smoke began to enter the room. The researchers then recorded the time in seconds before each participant left the room to report the smoke.

Researchers investigated whether cognitive-behavioral therapy reduces depression. They recruited 90 adults diagnosed with major depressive disorder and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition received twelve weekly sessions of cognitive-behavioral therapy. Participants in the other condition were placed on a waiting list for twelve weeks and were treated afterward. The researchers then recorded each participant's score on a standard depression questionnaire after twelve weeks.
Researchers collected data from 250 adults. For each one, they recorded resting heart rate and self-rated anxiety. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.38.

Researchers investigated whether spreading study sessions out improves long-term retention. They recruited 90 high school students and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition studied a list of 40 words in six ten-minute sessions on six different days. Participants in the other condition studied the same list in a single sixty-minute session. The researchers then recorded the number of words out of 40 that each participant recalled on a test one month later.

Researchers collected data from 300 families. For each one, they recorded the warmth of parenting, as rated by observers and the child's self-esteem score. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.48.

Researchers collected data from 600 university students. For each one, they recorded conscientiousness score on a personality inventory and grade point average. The correlation between the two measures was r = +0.35.

Researchers investigated whether an expected reward reduces children's later interest in drawing. They recruited 60 preschool children who enjoyed drawing and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Children in one condition were promised a certificate for drawing and received it. Children in the other condition drew with no reward mentioned. The researchers then recorded the number of minutes that each child chose to spend drawing during free time one week later.

Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They recruited 64 licensed drivers and randomly assigned each one to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers then recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

Read the summary of a hypothetical study, then answer parts A to F.

**Introduction.** Researchers investigated whether a phone conversation reduces what drivers notice. They hypothesized that phone use would affect attention to the road.

**Participants.** The sample was 64 licensed drivers, recruited from one city. All participants gave informed consent, were told they could withdraw at any time, and were debriefed afterward. The plan was approved by an institutional review board.

**Method.** The participants were randomly assigned to one of two conditions. Participants in one condition held a hands-free phone conversation while using a driving simulator. Participants in the other condition used the driving simulator without a phone. The researchers recorded the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

**Results.** The group that talked on the phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 11.4. The group that drove without a phone: mean road signs missed (out of 30) = 4.9. The difference was statistically significant (p = 0.01).

Use the three hypothetical sources to answer the question: **Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?**

**Source A.** In an experiment, 80 students were randomly assigned to be alone or with four other people when smoke began to enter the room. Participants who were alone reported the smoke after a mean of 58 seconds; those in groups took a mean of 196 seconds (p = 0.01), and many never reported it.

**Source B.** In interviews after a staged emergency, participants who had not helped often said that they 'assumed someone else had already called for help' or that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

**Source C.** Researchers observed 300 staged incidents in which a person dropped a bag of shopping in the street. Help was offered in 82 percent of incidents on quiet streets and in 41 percent of incidents on crowded streets.

questions.stem: A second study of a different pair of measures finds r = −0.80. Which relationship is stronger?

options.text: The relationship in the second study, because its coefficient is farther from zero
options.why: Correct. The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

options.text: The relationship in the first study, because its coefficient is closer to zero
options.why: A coefficient closer to zero shows a weaker relationship.

options.text: Neither, because relationships with different signs cannot be compared
options.why: Strength can be compared by distance from zero.

options.text: The relationship with the positive sign, whatever its size
options.why: The sign shows direction, not strength.

questions.explanation: The strength of a correlation is its distance from zero, whatever the sign.

questions.stem: What is the dependent variable in this study?

options.why: A hypothesis is a prediction, not a variable.
This was manipulated by the researchers: it is the independent variable.

options.text: The remembered speed of the cars
options.why: Correct. The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

options.text: The condition to which each one was assigned
options.why: This describes the independent variable.

questions.explanation: The dependent variable is the outcome that the researchers measured.

questions.stem: The more hours children spend watching television, the lower their grades tend to be. Which kind of relationship is this?

options.why: The directionality problem is the difficulty in a correlational study of knowing which variable influences the other.
A positive correlation is a relationship in which two variables rise and fall together.
Correct. A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.
A scatterplot is a graph in which each point shows one individual's values on two variables.

questions.explanation: A negative correlation is a relationship in which one variable rises as the other falls.

questions.stem: A therapist bluntly disputes his client's belief that 'everyone must like me or I am a failure.' Which therapy is this?

options.why: Correct. Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.
Dialectical behavior therapy is the therapy that teaches skills for tolerating distress and controlling emotions, often used for borderline personality disorder.
Cognitive-behavioral therapy is the therapy that combines changing self-defeating thoughts with changing behavior.
Cognitive restructuring is the technique of identifying irrational thoughts and replacing them with more realistic ones.

questions.explanation: Rational emotive behavior therapy is the confrontational cognitive therapy, developed by Ellis, that actively challenges a client's irrational beliefs.

questions.stem: The moment Lia hears that her company is closing, her heart races and adrenaline surges. Which phase of the general adaptation syndrome is this?

options.why: The resistance phase is the second phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body stays highly aroused to cope with a continuing stressor.
Correct. The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.
The general adaptation syndrome is Selye's three-phase description of the body's response to long-term stress: alarm, resistance and exhaustion.
The exhaustion phase is the third phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the body's resources run out and illness becomes more likely.

questions.explanation: The alarm reaction is the first phase of the general adaptation syndrome, in which the sympathetic nervous system is suddenly activated.

questions.stem: According to Freud, a person may be unable to recall a painful childhood event because the mind has blocked it from consciousness. What did Freud call this?

options.why: Retroactive interference is the disruption of older memories by new learning.
Encoding failure is forgetting that happens because the information never entered long-term memory.
Proactive interference is the disruption of new learning by older memories.
Correct. Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.explanation: Repression is in psychodynamic theory, the pushing of anxiety-arousing memories out of awareness.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the ICD?

options.text: The American Psychiatric Association's manual for classifying and diagnosing psychological disorders
options.why: That describes the DSM.

options.text: The criterion for a disorder that the behavior differs markedly from what a culture expects
options.why: That describes deviation from the social norm.

options.text: The World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders
options.why: Correct. This is what the ICD means.

options.text: The negative attitudes and discrimination directed at people who have a psychological disorder
options.why: That describes stigma.

questions.explanation: The ICD is the World Health Organization's international system for classifying all diseases, including mental disorders.

questions.stem: The drug group had lower anxiety scores. The difference was statistically significant. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The type of pill caused the difference in anxiety
options.why: Correct. With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

options.text: The hypothesis has been proved, so the study need not be repeated
options.why: Findings must be replicated; one study does not prove a hypothesis.

options.text: The type of pill and anxiety are related, but no cause can be inferred
options.why: That limit applies to correlational studies; this was an experiment.

options.text: The same result would be found in every group of people or animals
options.why: The sample limits how far the result can be generalized.

questions.explanation: With random assignment and a manipulated variable, an experiment supports a conclusion about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Can the researchers conclude that the number of hours of social media use per day causes a change in score on a depression questionnaire?

options.text: Yes, because the sample was large
options.why: A large sample does not turn a correlation into evidence of causation.

options.text: No, because correlations can only be calculated in experiments
options.why: Correlations are calculated in non-experimental studies.

options.text: No, because a correlation does not show cause and effect
options.why: Correct. Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

options.text: Yes, because the correlation is not zero
options.why: Any nonzero correlation still leaves the cause unknown.

questions.explanation: Without manipulating a variable and assigning subjects at random, other explanations cannot be ruled out.

questions.stem: Lena is so terrified of spiders that she will not enter any room where she has ever seen one. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Agoraphobia is the disorder in which a person fears and avoids public places from which escape might be difficult.
Correct. A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.
Panic disorder is the disorder in which a person has repeated, unexpected episodes of intense fear with physical symptoms such as chest pain.
Social anxiety disorder is the disorder in which a person has an intense fear of being judged or embarrassed in social situations.

questions.explanation: A specific phobia is the disorder in which a person has an intense, irrational fear of a particular object or situation.

questions.stem: Ben always plans ahead, meets every deadline and keeps his desk tidy. He would score high on which Big Five trait?

options.why: Agreeableness is the Big Five trait of being kind, trusting and cooperative.
Openness to experience is the Big Five trait of being imaginative, curious and willing to try new things.
Extraversion is the Big Five trait of being sociable, outgoing and energetic.
Correct. Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.explanation: Conscientiousness is the Big Five trait of being organized, careful and self-disciplined.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes metacognition?

options.text: The awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning
options.why: Correct. This is what metacognition means.

options.text: The improved recall that occurs in the same physical state as when the information was learned
options.why: That describes state-dependent memory.

options.text: The tendency to recall memories that match one's current mood
options.why: That describes mood-congruent memory.

options.text: The finding that practicing retrieval improves memory more than rereading
options.why: That describes the testing effect.

questions.explanation: Metacognition is the awareness and understanding of one's own thinking and learning.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a possible third variable that could explain the correlation?

options.text: The level of stress at home
options.why: Correct. A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.
This is one of the two variables that were measured.
This is the statistic, not a variable.

options.text: The average number of hours slept per night
options.why: This is one of the two variables that were measured.

questions.explanation: A third variable could influence both measures and so produce the correlation.

questions.stem: Before her wedding, Rosa feels nervous and excited, and the feeling gives her energy to prepare. Which kind of stress is this?

options.why: The fight-or-flight response is the response to stress in which the sympathetic nervous system prepares the body to attack or escape.
Correct. Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.
A stressor is an event or situation that a person sees as threatening or challenging.
The tend-and-befriend response is the response to stress of caring for others and seeking social support.

questions.explanation: Eustress is the positive, motivating stress that comes from a challenge.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement?

options.why: Pretend play is the play in which children act out imaginary roles and situations.
The imaginary audience is the belief of adolescents that everyone is watching and judging them.
Correct. The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.
Parallel play is the play of young children who play side by side without interacting.

questions.explanation: The social clock is a culture's preferred timing for life events such as marriage, parenthood and retirement.

questions.stem: Four studies of child development report these correlation coefficients: −0.61, −0.78, −0.93, +0.28. Which coefficient shows the weakest relationship?

options.why: Correct. Strength is the distance from zero, whatever the sign; +0.28 is closest to zero.
−0.78 is farther from zero.
−0.61 is farther from zero.
−0.93 is farther from zero.

questions.explanation: The sign of a correlation shows its direction; its distance from zero shows its strength. +0.28 is closest to zero.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes phantom limb sensation?

options.text: The sense of balance and head position, based on the semicircular canals of the inner ear
options.why: That describes the vestibular sense.

options.text: The sense of the position and movement of body parts, based on receptors in muscles and joints
options.why: That describes kinesthesis.

options.text: The theory that the spinal cord has a gate that can block pain signals or let them pass to the brain
options.why: That describes the gate control theory.

options.text: The feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated
options.why: Correct. This is what phantom limb sensation means.

questions.explanation: Phantom limb sensation is the feeling of pain or touch in a limb that has been amputated.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes nature?

options.text: The study of how the environment changes whether genes are expressed without changing the DNA itself
options.why: That describes epigenetics.

options.text: The influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes
options.why: Correct. This is what nature means.

options.text: Research that compares adopted children with their biological and adoptive relatives
options.why: That describes an adoption study.

options.text: Research that compares identical and fraternal twins to estimate the influence of heredity
options.why: That describes a twin study.

questions.explanation: Nature is the influence of inherited genetic factors on behavior and mental processes.

questions.stem: Olga, who loves a certain band, is surprised to learn that most of her classmates have never heard of it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Collectivism is the cultural pattern that gives priority to the goals of the group and defines identity by group membership.
Conformity is the adjusting of behavior or thinking to match a group standard.
Correct. The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.
A social trap is a situation in which people who each pursue their own interest end up harming everyone.

questions.explanation: The false consensus effect is the tendency to overestimate how many other people share our opinions and behaviors.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes sound localization?

options.text: The theory that we hear different pitches because different sound waves trigger different places on the cochlea's membrane
options.why: That describes place theory.

options.text: The ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears
options.why: Correct. This is what sound localization means.

options.text: Hearing loss caused by damage to the eardrum or the bones of the middle ear
options.why: That describes conduction deafness.

options.text: The theory that we hear pitch because the rate of nerve impulses matches the frequency of the sound
options.why: That describes frequency theory.

questions.explanation: Sound localization is the ability to tell where a sound comes from, using differences in timing and loudness between the two ears.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes an avoidance-avoidance conflict?

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options
options.why: Correct. This is what an avoidance-avoidance conflict means.

options.text: A conflict in which one option has both attractive and unattractive features
options.why: That describes an approach-avoidance conflict.

options.text: The desire to do something for its own sake, because it is enjoyable or satisfying
options.why: That describes intrinsic motivation.

options.text: A conflict in which a person must choose between two attractive options
options.why: That describes an approach-approach conflict.

questions.explanation: An avoidance-avoidance conflict is a conflict in which a person must choose between two unattractive options.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes in-group bias?

options.text: The tendency to favor the members of one's own group
options.why: Correct. This is what in-group bias means.

options.text: The discomfort a person feels when their actions and attitudes conflict, which motivates a change in one of them
options.why: That describes cognitive dissonance.

options.text: The tendency to hold on to a belief even after the evidence for it has been discredited
options.why: That describes belief perseverance.

options.text: The tendency to search for and favor information that supports what one already believes
options.why: That describes confirmation bias.

questions.explanation: In-group bias is the tendency to favor the members of one's own group.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep?

options.why: Bipolar II disorder is the disorder in which a person alternates between depression and a milder form of mania called hypomania.
Correct. Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.
Major depressive disorder is the disorder in which a person has at least two weeks of depressed mood or loss of interest, with other symptoms such as changes in sleep and appetite.
Bipolar I disorder is the disorder in which a person has full manic episodes, usually alternating with depression.

questions.explanation: Mania is a state of extreme energy, overconfidence, racing thoughts and little need for sleep.

questions.stem: Mila constantly seeks out unfamiliar music, foreign films and trips to places she has never been. Which form of sensation seeking is this?

options.why: Boredom susceptibility is the form of sensation seeking that involves a strong dislike of repetition and routine.
Correct. Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.
Thrill and adventure seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for risky physical activities.
Disinhibition is the form of sensation seeking that involves a loss of self-restraint, as at wild parties.

questions.explanation: Experience seeking is the form of sensation seeking that involves a desire for new experiences through travel, art and unusual lifestyles.

questions.stem: During adolescence, Luis grows facial hair and his voice deepens. These changes are examples of which of the following?

options.why: Menopause is the natural end of menstruation and of the ability to reproduce, usually around age 50.
Primary sex characteristics is the body structures, such as ovaries and testes, that make reproduction possible.
Spermarche is a boy's first ejaculation.
Correct. Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.explanation: Secondary sex characteristics is the nonreproductive traits of sexual maturity, such as body hair and a deeper voice.

questions.stem: A child's schooling is disrupted by a pandemic at age eight. In ecological systems theory, the timing of this event is part of which system?

options.why: The macrosystem is in ecological systems theory, the cultural values, laws and customs that surround a child.
The exosystem is in ecological systems theory, the settings that affect a child indirectly, such as a parent's workplace.
Correct. The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.
The microsystem is in ecological systems theory, the groups that have direct contact with the child, such as family and school.

questions.explanation: The chronosystem is in ecological systems theory, the life stage and historical events that affect a child.

questions.stem: Patients given a sugar pill report less pain simply because they believe they have taken a painkiller. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: The experimental group is the group in an experiment that receives the treatment being tested.
A double-blind procedure is a procedure in which neither the participants nor the researchers who deal with them know who is in which condition.
The control group is the group in an experiment that does not receive the treatment and is used for comparison.
Correct. The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.

questions.explanation: The placebo effect is an improvement that results from a person's expectation of a treatment rather than from the treatment itself.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the absolute threshold?

options.text: The conversion of physical energy, such as light or sound, into neural impulses
options.why: That describes transduction.

options.text: The way one sense influences another, as when smell affects taste
options.why: That describes sensory interaction.

options.text: The reduced sensitivity that follows constant, unchanging stimulation
options.why: That describes sensory adaptation.

options.text: The weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time
options.why: Correct. This is what the absolute threshold means.

questions.explanation: The absolute threshold is the weakest level of a stimulus that a person can detect half of the time.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes group therapy?

options.text: The therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support
options.why: Correct. This is what group therapy means.

options.text: A state of heightened suggestibility that can help reduce pain and anxiety but does not reliably recover memories
options.why: That describes hypnosis.

options.text: The psychodynamic technique of analyzing dreams to uncover unconscious wishes and conflicts
options.why: That describes dream interpretation.

options.text: The psychodynamic technique in which the client says whatever comes to mind
options.why: That describes free association.

questions.explanation: Group therapy is the therapy in which several clients meet together with a therapist and benefit from each other's support.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes self-report bias?

options.text: The tendency, after learning an outcome, to believe one would have predicted it
options.why: That describes hindsight bias.

options.text: The inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings
options.why: Correct. This is what self-report bias means.

options.text: The influence of a researcher's expectations on the results of a study
options.why: That describes experimenter bias.

options.text: The tendency of participants to answer in a way that makes them look good
options.why: That describes social desirability bias.

questions.explanation: Self-report bias is the inaccuracy that arises when people describe their own behavior or feelings.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes relative deprivation?

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as temporary, specific and caused by outside factors
options.why: That describes an optimistic explanatory style.

options.text: The tendency to credit our successes to ourselves and blame our failures on outside factors
options.why: That describes the self-serving bias.

options.text: The habit of explaining bad events as lasting, affecting everything and caused by oneself
options.why: That describes a pessimistic explanatory style.

options.text: The feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with
options.why: Correct. This is what relative deprivation means.

questions.explanation: Relative deprivation is the feeling of being worse off than the people one compares oneself with.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes discrimination?

options.text: Unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members
options.why: Correct. This is what discrimination means.

options.text: An attitude that a person holds without being aware of it
options.why: That describes an implicit attitude.

options.text: An unjustified negative attitude toward a group and its members
options.why: That describes prejudice.

options.text: The tendency to believe that people get what they deserve
options.why: That describes the just-world phenomenon.

questions.explanation: Discrimination is unjustified negative behavior toward a group and its members.

questions.stem: Which statement about the results is best supported?

options.text: The study shows that the two conditions always give identical results
options.why: A non-significant result does not show that there is no effect at all.

options.text: The independent variable had a large effect
options.why: The averages are close and the difference is not significant.

options.text: The difference between the groups is statistically significant
options.why: A p value of 0.41 is far above 0.05.

options.text: The difference between the groups is not statistically significant, so it could easily be due to chance
options.why: Correct. A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.explanation: A p value above 0.05 means a difference this size would often occur by chance alone.

questions.stem: People who move next to a railway are woken by trains at first but soon sleep through the noise. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.
One-trial conditioning is learning that happens after a single pairing of two stimuli.
Biological preparedness is the inborn readiness to learn some associations, such as taste and nausea, more easily than others.
Counterconditioning is the replacing of an unwanted response to a stimulus with a new response, by pairing the stimulus with something pleasant.

questions.explanation: Habituation is the decrease in response to a stimulus that is presented over and over.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes priming?

options.text: The mistaken belief that a random event is more likely because it has not happened recently
options.why: That describes the gambler's fallacy.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how easily examples come to mind
options.why: That describes the availability heuristic.

options.text: The judging of how likely something is by how well it matches a prototype, while ignoring base rates
options.why: That describes the representativeness heuristic.

options.text: The activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior
options.why: Correct. This is what priming means.

questions.explanation: Priming is the activation, often without awareness, of certain associations that then influence perception or behavior.

questions.stem: A group of people who mildly support a policy discuss it together and end up strongly supporting it. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Deindividuation is the loss of self-awareness and self-restraint in group situations that provide arousal and anonymity.
Social facilitation is the improved performance on simple or well-learned tasks in the presence of others.
Groupthink is the kind of thinking in which the desire for agreement in a group overrides a realistic evaluation of alternatives.
Correct. Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.

questions.explanation: Group polarization is the strengthening of a group's existing opinions after the members discuss them.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes assimilation?

options.text: The best or most typical example of a category
options.why: That describes a prototype.

options.text: A mental grouping of similar objects, events, ideas or people
options.why: That describes a concept.

options.text: The interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema
options.why: Correct. This is what assimilation means.

options.text: The changing of an existing schema to fit new information
options.why: That describes accommodation.

questions.explanation: Assimilation is the interpretation of a new experience in terms of an existing schema.

questions.stem: Which of the following would be a confounding variable in this study?

options.text: The two groups differed in the reporting of an emergency at the end of the study
options.why: That is the dependent variable, the result being measured.

options.text: The rooms used for the groups of five were much noisier
options.why: Correct. It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

options.text: Each one was assigned to a condition at random
options.why: Random assignment reduces confounding; it is not a confound.

options.text: One group differed from the other in the number of other people present
options.why: That is the independent variable itself.

questions.explanation: It differs between the groups along with the independent variable, so it could explain the results instead.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a gender role?

options.text: A person's own sense of being male, female, neither or some combination
options.why: That describes gender identity.

options.text: The direction of a person's enduring sexual attraction
options.why: That describes sexual orientation.

options.text: The set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women
options.why: Correct. This is what a gender role means.

options.text: The socially and culturally influenced attitudes, feelings and behaviors that a culture links to being a boy, girl, man or woman
options.why: That describes gender.

questions.explanation: A gender role is the set of behaviors that a culture expects of men or of women.

questions.stem: What is the independent variable in this study?

options.why: This is a procedure for forming the groups, not a variable.

options.text: The number of participants in the study
options.why: This is the sample size, not a variable the researchers changed.
Correct. The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.
This was measured, not manipulated: it is the dependent variable.

questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor the researchers changed between the two conditions.

questions.stem: A female moth releases a chemical into the air that attracts males from far away. What is this chemical called?

options.why: Correct. A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.
Olfaction is the sense of smell, the only sense that does not pass through the thalamus first.
Gustation is the sense of taste, which detects sweet, sour, salty, bitter, umami and oleogustus.
A supertaster is a person with more taste receptors than average, who experiences tastes more intensely.

questions.explanation: A pheromone is a chemical signal released by one member of a species that affects the behavior of others.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory?

options.why: The central executive is the part of working memory that directs attention and coordinates the other parts.
The visuospatial sketchpad is the part of working memory that briefly holds images and spatial information.
The phonological loop is the part of working memory that briefly holds spoken and written words.
Correct. Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.explanation: Long-term potentiation is the strengthening of the connections between neurons after repeated activation, which is the biological basis of memory.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes dissociative identity disorder?

options.text: The disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times
options.why: Correct. This is what dissociative identity disorder means.

options.text: The disorder in which a person cannot throw away possessions, so that living spaces become cluttered
options.why: That describes hoarding disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has unwanted repeated thoughts and feels driven to perform repeated actions
options.why: That describes obsessive-compulsive disorder.

options.text: The disorder in which a person has flashbacks, nightmares, watchfulness and avoidance for more than a month after a terrifying event
options.why: That describes posttraumatic stress disorder.

questions.explanation: Dissociative identity disorder is the disorder in which a person shows two or more distinct personalities that take control at different times.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care?

options.why: Correct. Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.
Evidence-based practice is the choosing of treatments on the basis of research, clinical skill and the client's own values.
A meta-analysis is a statistical procedure that combines the results of many studies to reach an overall conclusion.
The therapeutic alliance is the bond of trust and cooperation between therapist and client.

questions.explanation: Deinstitutionalization is the movement, begun in the 1950s, of patients out of psychiatric hospitals and into community care.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate?

options.why: Insight learning is the sudden realization of the solution to a problem.
Latent learning is learning that takes place without reinforcement and is not shown until there is a reason to show it.
A cognitive map is a mental picture of the layout of one's surroundings.
Correct. Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.

questions.explanation: Modeling is the process of demonstrating a behavior that others then observe and imitate.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Another research team repeats this study with new subjects and obtains the same result. What is this called?

options.why: That is how subjects are placed in conditions.
That is an in-depth study of one individual.
Correct. Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.
That is explaining the study to participants afterward.

questions.explanation: Replication is repeating a study to see whether the finding holds.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the directionality problem in this study?

options.text: It is unclear whether the first measure influences the second or the second influences the first
options.why: Correct. A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

options.text: It is unclear whether the two measures were recorded
options.why: Both measures were recorded.

options.text: It is unclear how many people took part
options.why: The sample size is stated.

options.text: It is unclear whether the correlation is positive or negative
options.why: The sign of r shows the direction of the relationship.

questions.explanation: A correlation cannot show which variable, if either, comes first.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes?

options.why: Interposition is the monocular depth cue in which an object that partly blocks another is seen as closer.
Correct. Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.
Relative clarity is the monocular depth cue in which hazy objects are seen as farther away than sharp ones.
Linear perspective is the monocular depth cue in which parallel lines seem to meet in the distance.

questions.explanation: Retinal disparity is the binocular depth cue based on the difference between the images in the two eyes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness?

options.why: Correct. Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.
The cochlea is the coiled, fluid-filled tube in the inner ear where sound waves become neural impulses.
Frequency is the number of sound waves per second, which determines pitch.
Wavelength is the distance from one wave peak to the next, which determines the hue of light.

questions.explanation: Amplitude is the height of a sound wave, which determines loudness.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information?

options.why: The misinformation effect is the distortion of a memory by misleading information received after the event.
Correct. Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.
Imagination inflation is the increased confidence that an event happened after repeatedly imagining it.
Source amnesia is the inability to remember where, when or how a piece of information was learned.

questions.explanation: Constructive memory is the building of a memory at retrieval from stored pieces, expectations and later information.

questions.stem: Five-year-old Ivy rarely makes eye contact, struggles with conversation, rocks back and forth and is upset by any change in routine. Which disorder does this suggest?

options.why: Binge-eating disorder is the eating disorder in which a person repeatedly eats very large amounts and feels distress, without purging afterward.
Correct. Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.
Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by inattention, hyperactivity and impulsiveness.
Bulimia nervosa is the eating disorder in which a person binges on food and then makes up for it by vomiting, fasting or excessive exercise.

questions.explanation: Autism spectrum disorder is the neurodevelopmental disorder marked by difficulties with social communication and by repetitive behaviors or narrow interests.

questions.stem: A researcher stores survey answers under code numbers so that no answer can be linked to a name. Which ethical requirement is this?

options.why: Protection from harm is the requirement that researchers keep the physical and psychological risks to participants as low as possible.
Correct. Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.
Informed assent is the agreement of a minor to take part in a study, given in addition to a parent's consent.
Debriefing is the explaining of a study's purpose, and any deception, to participants after it ends.

questions.explanation: Confidentiality is the keeping private of participants' identities and data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons?

options.why: Correct. Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.
Sensory neurons is the neurons that carry incoming information from the sense receptors to the brain and spinal cord.
The reflex arc is the simple automatic pathway in which the spinal cord produces a response before the brain is aware of the stimulus.
Interneurons is the neurons inside the brain and spinal cord that pass messages between sensory inputs and motor outputs.

questions.explanation: Glial cells is the cells that support, nourish, insulate and protect neurons.

questions.stem: In one culture, people are expected to hide their disappointment in public; in another, they show it openly. This difference reflects which of the following?

options.why: The facial-feedback hypothesis is the idea that the expression on a person's face can influence the emotion the person feels.
The broaden-and-build theory is the theory that positive emotions widen a person's awareness and help build lasting skills and resources.
Universal emotions is the basic emotions, such as happiness, sadness, fear and anger, whose facial expressions are recognized across cultures.
Correct. A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.

questions.explanation: A display rule is a cultural rule about which emotions may be shown, when and to whom.

questions.stem: To read small print, a person moves their eyes so the words fall on the point of sharpest vision. What is this point called?

options.why: The retina is the light-sensitive inner surface at the back of the eye that contains the receptor cells.
Rods is the receptor cells that detect black, white and gray and work in dim light and peripheral vision.
Correct. The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.
The blind spot is the point where the optic nerve leaves the eye, which has no receptor cells.

questions.explanation: The fovea is the central point of the retina, where cones are packed most densely and vision is sharpest.

questions.stem: Why is this study not an experiment?

options.why: Experiments also test hypotheses.

options.text: The researchers did not manipulate a variable or randomly assign anyone to conditions
options.why: Correct. An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.
Sample size does not determine the research method.
Experiments also use numerical data.

questions.explanation: An experiment requires a manipulated independent variable and random assignment.

questions.stem: A crawling infant refuses to cross a sheet of glass over what looks like a steep drop. Which apparatus is being used?

options.why: A critical period is a limited time early in life when certain experiences must occur for normal development.
Imprinting is the process by which some animals form a strong attachment to the first moving object they see.
Correct. The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.
Gross motor skills is the movements that use large muscles, such as crawling, walking and jumping.

questions.explanation: The visual cliff is the laboratory apparatus with a glass-covered drop that is used to test depth perception in infants.

questions.stem: Why did the researchers assign the children to the two conditions at random?

options.text: So that the results could be generalized to the whole population
options.why: That is the purpose of random sampling, not random assignment.

options.text: So that nobody would know the hypothesis
options.why: That describes a blind procedure.

options.text: So that the two groups would be similar at the start, and any difference could be attributed to the independent variable
options.why: Correct. Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

options.text: So that the study would have more participants
options.why: Random assignment does not change the sample size.

questions.explanation: Random assignment spreads individual differences evenly across the conditions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions?

options.why: Correct. The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.
The formal operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 12 on, in which people can reason about abstract and hypothetical ideas.
The preoperational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 2 to 7, in which children use words and images but cannot yet reason logically.
The concrete operational stage is Piaget's stage from about age 7 to 11, in which children think logically about real objects and events.

questions.explanation: The sensorimotor stage is Piaget's stage from birth to about age 2, in which infants know the world through senses and actions.

questions.stem: A researcher gives one randomly chosen group a vitamin and another group a sugar pill, then compares their memory scores. Which research method is this?

options.why: Correct. An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.
Replication is the repeating of a study with different participants to see whether the finding holds.
Naturalistic observation is the research method of watching and recording behavior in its natural setting without interfering.
An operational definition is a statement of exactly how a variable is measured or manipulated in a study.

questions.explanation: An experiment is the research method in which a researcher manipulates a variable and randomly assigns participants, which allows conclusions about cause and effect.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes reversibility?

options.text: The belief of young children that lifeless objects have feelings and intentions
options.why: That describes animism.

options.text: The difficulty that young children have in taking another person's point of view
options.why: That describes egocentrism.

options.text: The understanding that things continue to exist when they are out of sight
options.why: That describes object permanence.

options.text: The understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state
options.why: Correct. This is what reversibility means.

questions.explanation: Reversibility is the understanding that an action can be undone to return things to their original state.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function?

options.why: A case study is an in-depth study of one individual, such as a patient with unusual brain damage.
Neuroplasticity is the brain's ability to change by reorganizing after damage or building new pathways through experience.
An fMRI is a scan that shows brain activity by tracking blood flow.
Correct. Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.explanation: Lesioning is the destruction of a small area of brain tissue to study its function.

questions.stem: Without considering any alternatives, Ravi plans to join the family business because his parents always expected it. Which identity status is this?

options.why: Identity moratorium is the identity status of a person who is actively exploring options but has not yet made a commitment.
Identity diffusion is the identity status of a person who has neither explored options nor made a commitment.
Identity achievement is the identity status of a person who has explored options and made a commitment.
Correct. Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.explanation: Identity foreclosure is the identity status of a person who has made a commitment without exploring options.

questions.stem: To learn forty new vocabulary words, Felix must concentrate and rehearse them. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Structural encoding is the shallow encoding of a word based on its appearance.
Explicit memory is the memory of facts and experiences that a person can consciously recall and state.
Implicit memory is the memory of skills and learned associations that is retained without conscious recall.
Correct. Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

questions.explanation: Effortful processing is the encoding that requires attention and conscious effort.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it?

options.why: Emotion-focused coping is the reducing of stress by managing one's emotional reaction rather than the stressor.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure, which is made more likely by chronic stress.
Correct. Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.
Immune suppression is the weakening of the body's defenses against illness during long-term stress.

questions.explanation: Problem-focused coping is the reducing of stress by changing the stressor itself or the way one deals with it.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes regression?

options.text: The defense mechanism of pushing anxiety-arousing thoughts and memories out of awareness
options.why: That describes repression.

options.text: The defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development
options.why: Correct. This is what regression means.

options.text: The defense mechanism of turning unacceptable impulses into socially valued activities
options.why: That describes sublimation.

options.text: The defense mechanism of acting in the opposite way to one's unacceptable impulses
options.why: That describes reaction formation.

questions.explanation: Regression is the defense mechanism of retreating to behavior from an earlier stage of development.

questions.stem: A patient with damage to the visual cortex says she sees nothing, yet she walks around obstacles in a hallway. Which condition does she have?

options.why: Correct. Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.
The trichromatic theory is the theory that the retina has three types of color receptors, sensitive to red, green and blue.
Dichromatism is a form of color vision deficiency in which one of the three types of cones does not work.
The opponent-process theory is the theory that color is processed in opposing pairs: red–green, blue–yellow and black–white.

questions.explanation: Blindsight is the ability to respond to visual information without consciously seeing it.

questions.stem: After the study, the researchers explained its full purpose to every participant and answered their questions. What is this called?

options.why: A placebo is an inactive treatment.
Correct. Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.
Replication is repeating a study.
Consent is obtained before the study.

questions.explanation: Debriefing explains the study, including any deception, once it is over.

questions.stem: A child gets out of bed during deep sleep, walks to the kitchen, and remembers nothing in the morning. Which sleep disorder is this?

options.why: Sleep apnea is a sleep disorder in which breathing repeatedly stops during sleep, causing brief awakenings.
Insomnia is a sleep disorder with ongoing difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
Narcolepsy is a sleep disorder with sudden, uncontrollable attacks of sleep, often straight into REM sleep.
Correct. Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.explanation: Somnambulism is sleepwalking, which occurs during deep NREM sleep.

questions.stem: A dog already salivates to a tone. A light is then repeatedly shown just before the tone, and the dog begins to salivate to the light. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.
Stimulus discrimination is the learned ability to respond to the conditioned stimulus but not to similar stimuli.
Stimulus generalization is the tendency to respond to stimuli that are similar to the conditioned stimulus.
Extinction is the weakening of a conditioned response when the conditioned stimulus is repeatedly presented alone.

questions.explanation: Higher-order conditioning is the pairing of a new neutral stimulus with an existing conditioned stimulus to create a second conditioned stimulus.

questions.stem: Which of the following is best described as Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships?

options.why: Identity versus role confusion is Erikson's stage in adolescence, in which teenagers work out who they are.
Integrity versus despair is Erikson's stage in late adulthood, in which people look back on life with satisfaction or regret.
Correct. Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.
Generativity versus stagnation is Erikson's stage in middle adulthood, in which people seek to contribute to the world through family and work.

questions.explanation: Intimacy versus isolation is Erikson's stage in young adulthood, in which people seek close, lasting relationships.

questions.stem: An eight-year-old answers the questions that a typical ten-year-old can answer. On Binet's test, ten is the child's what?

options.why: The intelligence quotient is originally, mental age divided by chronological age and multiplied by 100.
Correct. Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.
Multiple intelligences is the theory that people have several independent kinds of intelligence, such as musical and interpersonal.
The Flynn effect is the steady rise in average intelligence test scores over the generations.

questions.explanation: Mental age is the level of performance typical of a certain chronological age on an intelligence test.

questions.stem: Immediately after hearing a shopping list, Ken can repeat the final three items but not the middle ones. This best illustrates which of the following?

options.why: Correct. The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.
The primacy effect is the tendency to remember the first items in a list well.
The serial position effect is the tendency to remember the first and last items in a list better than the middle ones.
The spacing effect is the finding that study spread over time produces better long-term memory than study crammed together.

questions.explanation: The recency effect is the tendency to remember the last items in a list well.

questions.stem: Scores on a test are normally distributed with a mean of 100 and a standard deviation of 20. About what percentage of scores are below 80?

options.why: This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
Correct. 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is below.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.
This does not match the 68–95 rule for a normal distribution.

questions.explanation: 68% lie within one standard deviation, leaving 32% outside, half of which (16%) is below. (80 and 120 are one standard deviation from the mean; 60 and 140 are two.)

questions.title: Article analysis: a study of attention to the road

parts.prompt: Identify the research method used in the study.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the method as an experiment.
rubric.example: The study is an experiment: the researchers manipulated a variable and randomly assigned the subjects to conditions.

parts.prompt: State the operational definition of attention to the road.

rubric.criterion: States how the variable was measured in this study.
rubric.example: Attention to the road was defined as the number of road signs out of 30 that each participant failed to notice.

parts.prompt: Describe the meaning of the difference between the two group averages.

rubric.criterion: Accurately describes which group scored higher or lower and what that means for the variable measured.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. On average, the value was 11.4 for the group that talked on the phone and 4.9 for the group that drove without a phone, and a p value of 0.01 means a difference this large is unlikely to be due to chance.

parts.prompt: Identify at least one ethical guideline applied by the researchers.

rubric.criterion: Identifies an ethical guideline that the summary shows was followed.
rubric.example: Informed consent: participants agreed to take part after being told about the study. (Also acceptable: debriefing; the right to withdraw; approval by an institutional review board.)

parts.prompt: Explain the extent to which the research findings may or may not be generalizable, using specific and relevant evidence from the study.

rubric.criterion: Explains a limit (or strength) of generalizability with reference to the sample.
rubric.example: The sample was 64 licensed drivers from one city, so the findings may not apply to people of other ages, cultures or backgrounds. Because the sample was not randomly selected from a wider population, it may not be representative.

parts.prompt: Explain how at least one of the research findings supports or refutes the researchers' hypothesis.

rubric.criterion: Uses a specific finding from the study as evidence.
rubric.example: The phone group missed more road signs. (11.4 compared with 4.9).

rubric.criterion: Explains how the finding supports the hypothesis, using a psychological concept.
rubric.example: This supports the hypothesis that phone use affects attention to the road. Because subjects were randomly assigned, the difference can be attributed to phone use. The finding illustrates selective attention and inattentional blindness: attention is limited, so people fail to notice visible objects when attention is elsewhere.

questions.title: Evidence-based question: Why do people sometimes fail to help in an emergency?

parts.prompt: Propose a specific and defensible claim, based in psychological science, that responds to the question.

rubric.criterion: States a claim that answers the question and can be supported by the sources.
rubric.example: People are less likely to help when others are present, because each person feels less responsible and looks to others to decide how to act.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using at least one piece of specific and relevant evidence from one of the sources. (ii) Explain how the evidence supports your claim, using a psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding learned in AP Psychology.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from one source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source A, participants who were alone reported smoke after 58 seconds, but those in groups of five took 196 seconds.

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through the bystander effect and diffusion of responsibility: when others are present, each person feels less personal responsibility to act.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a psychological concept in the explanation.
rubric.example: The concept must be named and applied correctly, as in the model explanation.

parts.prompt: (i) Support your claim using an additional piece of specific and relevant evidence from a different source. (ii) Explain how this evidence supports your claim, using a different psychological perspective, theory, concept or research finding.

rubric.criterion: Uses specific, relevant evidence from a different source and names the source.
rubric.example: In Source B, participants said that 'nobody else looked worried, so it could not be serious.'

rubric.criterion: Explains how the evidence supports the claim.
rubric.example: This supports the claim through informational social influence: in an unclear situation, people use the behavior of others as evidence of what is happening, so if nobody reacts, each person concludes there is no emergency.

rubric.criterion: Correctly applies a different psychological concept from the one used in part B.
rubric.example: The concept must differ from the one used in part B and be applied correctly.
